title: Win32 Job primitive: pinned Rust crate, call-table seam, RAII handles, Job create/configure/query
description:
SPIDR child 1 of 2, split from task-ea76e0cf9bdb4f1888aaa9e49323c782 by architect-cb476f76 on plan shape, not on lines: the parent needs 12 distinct files against the daemon's hard ceiling of 10, and its job and process modules would each breach the 250-line per-file target. Sibling: child 2 (suspended process, JOB_LIST membership, identity, resume, unwind, real-Windows acceptance), which depends on this task.

Objective: land the first Rust in this monorepo as a version-pinned crate, plus the injectable Win32 call-table seam and RAII handle discipline every later Job operation builds on, plus the Job object itself.

MEASURED 2026-08-09 at HEAD 7d9efc9, not taken from the parent description: packages/runner/src/platform/windows/native does not exist; `find -name Cargo.toml` outside node_modules returns nothing, so this is the first Rust in the repo; `rustc --version` reports exactly 1.96.0 (ac68faa20 2026-05-25) and cargo 1.96.0, matching the pin; a scratch `cargo add windows-sys@=0.61.2 --features Win32_System_JobObjects` resolved against crates.io and locked, so the registry is reachable and both the version and the feature exist.

Deliverable: packages/runner/src/platform/windows/native/ containing Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, rust-toolchain.toml pinning rustc 1.96.0, and src/lib.rs, src/win32.rs (call-table trait, real windows-sys implementation, closed native-operation enum), src/handle.rs (RAII owned handle closing exactly once), src/job.rs (unnamed Job creation; set LimitFlags to exactly JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE with neither breakaway flag; query the flags back and refuse on mismatch; TerminateJobObject; ActiveProcesses query; close). Plus tests/job_sweep.rs driving the injected call table.

NOT in scope and deliberately left to child 2: CreateProcessW, PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_JOB_LIST, AssignProcessToJobObject, membership or identity proof, ResumeThread, wait, partial-construction unwind, and real-Windows integration tests. Also out of scope, as in the parent: Node/stdio framing, JavaScript validation, Claude discovery/grants, daemon/store authority, receipts, and any public @moe/runner export.

Production consumer: child 2, then task-af3d7bc8af2146cf92d98557ed0e90c0 (Windows Job broker protocol, which names the parent explicitly), then task-4d1f8ba54cb6476c930c46b413f882aa.

Verification: cargo test --locked --manifest-path packages/runner/src/platform/windows/native/Cargo.toml --target-dir dist/windows-job-native -p moe-windows-job-core && cargo build --locked --release --manifest-path packages/runner/src/platform/windows/native/Cargo.toml --target-dir dist/windows-job-native -p moe-windows-job-core
definitionOfDone: packages/runner/src/platform/windows/native pins rustc 1.96.0 in committed rust-toolchain.toml and windows-sys to exactly =0.61.2 in committed Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock bytes; the locked test and release-build commands both exit 0 on supported Windows.
The build writes only into dist/windows-job-native and no target directory, executable, debug artifact, probe file, or generated evidence file is committed; dist/ is confirmed ignored by git.

An unnamed Job is created, LimitFlags are set to exactly JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE with neither JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_BREAKAWAY_OK nor SILENT_BREAKAWAY_OK, and the flags are queried back and compared; a mismatch refuses with the exact stable native operation code rather than proceeding.

Every Win32 call goes through the injectable call table; failures carry the closed operation enum plus the numeric Win32 error only, and never echo executable, argv, cwd, environment, or raw handle values.

An injected call-table sweep exercises each of the create, configure, query-back, terminate, active-process-query and close arms, asserts the exact stable operation code per arm, and asserts a nonzero exact case count so a sweep that generates zero cases cannot pass.

Each owned handle closes exactly once on every success and failure path, proven by a drop-counting call table; a close whose outcome is unknown is retained as uncertain and never converted to success.
Every Rust production source is <=250 physical lines; child 2 (suspended process, membership, resume, unwind, real-Windows acceptance) is named as the consumer that composes this primitive.
taskRails: Use Microsoft Job Object semantics; supported floor is Windows 10 / Server 2016.
Native failures carry a closed operation enum and numeric Win32 error only; never echo executable, argv, cwd, environment, or raw handle values.
Keep every Rust production source focused, target <=250 physical lines and split before 400; commit Cargo.lock but never Cargo target output or binaries.
This is a native primitive, not authority: no @moe/runner root export, Claude policy, activation grant, daemon/store call, or evidence claim.

Do not implement any process-creation, membership, assignment, identity, resume, wait or unwind behaviour here; those belong to child 2 and duplicating them creates a collision in the shared worktree.

implementationPlan.description: TDD red: write tests/job_sweep.rs against the not-yet-existing API. Define a scripted test call table implementing the Win32Calls trait that records an ordered call log and can be programmed to fail at any single arm. Declare a frozen CASES table with exactly one entry per failable arm -- CreateJobObject, SetInformation, QueryInformation, TerminateJob, QueryAccounting, CloseHandle -- each naming the arm, the injected Win32 error, and the exact expected NativeOp. Assert CASES.len() == 6 and that the set of NativeOp values the sweep produced equals the full NativeOp set, so a sweep that silently generates zero cases cannot pass (epic rail 6). Every failure assertion checks the exact NativeOp AND the exact numeric Win32 code -- never merely that the call returned Err. Add: a success case asserting the exact call ORDER is create, set, query, compare (no terminate or close in between); a case where QueryInformation returns LimitFlags equal to KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE|BREAKAWAY_OK and asserting the mismatch is REFUSED, which pins that the comparison is exact equality and not a bitwise-contains; and a drop-counting assertion that each acquired handle is closed exactly once across both the success and every failure path. Tests must fail to compile now -- that is the red.
implementationPlan.note:
TDD red confirmed by compiler, not by assumption:

  error[E0432]: unresolved imports `moe_windows_job_core::Job`, `::NativeError`,
    `::NativeOp`, `::RawHandle`, `::Win32Calls`, `::REQUIRED_LIMIT_FLAGS`
  error: could not compile `moe-windows-job-core` (test "job_sweep")
  EXIT 101

All six names the sweep needs are absent, so nothing here can be passing by accident yet.

WHAT THE SWEEP PINS (7 tests):
1. sweep_pins_the_exact_op_and_code_for_every_arm - drives all 6 arms, asserts exact NativeOp AND exact numeric Win32 code per arm.
2. required_flags_are_kill_on_close_alone - REQUIRED_LIMIT_FLAGS == 0x2000 and carries no breakaway bit.
3. successful_creation_calls_create_set_query_in_order - exact call log ["create","set","query"], no terminate/close in between.
4. query_back_refuses_flags_that_also_carry_breakaway - the equality-vs-contains guard.
5. first_failure_survives_the_cleanup_close - a cleanup close must not overwrite the operational error.
6. every_acquired_handle_closes_exactly_once_on_every_path - success, drop-without-close, and all 6 failure paths.
7. a_failed_close_is_never_laundered_into_success.

THREE GUARDS AGAINST THE VACUITY MODES EPIC RAIL 6 NAMES:
- CASES.len() == 6 asserted, so deleting a case reddens instead of silently shrinking the sweep.
- The produced NativeOp set is compared against production `NativeOp::ALL`, NOT against CASES. Comparing the sweep's output to its own input would be self-derived and prove nothing.
- Each case carries a DISTINCT Win32 code (5/87/24/1314/6/998). With a shared code, "reported the right arm" and "reported the right code by coincidence" are indistinguishable.

BREAKAWAY_OK is spelled as the literal 0x0800 in the test rather than imported from production, deliberately: if the mismatch case imported the same constant the production comparison uses, both could drift together and the test would follow the defect.

API SURFACE THIS FREEZES for steps 3-6: NativeOp{CreateJobObject,SetInformation,QueryInformation,TerminateJob,QueryAccounting,CloseHandle} + NativeOp::ALL; NativeError::new/op()/code(); RawHandle::new/value(); Win32Calls with 6 methods taking RawHandle (not bare isize); REQUIRED_LIMIT_FLAGS; Job::create/terminate/active_processes/close.

Two semantics the tests pin that the implementation must honour: a flag MISMATCH refuses with op=QueryInformation and code=0, because it is a refusal rather than a Win32 failure; and a FAILED close still sets the closed flag so Drop cannot retry it, which is what makes "exactly once" true on the failure path too.

Re-ran from the repo root. Recording it because a relative --manifest-path silently measures a different tree depending on cwd, and here it failed loudly only because nothing resolved.

implementationPlan.description: Implement src/win32.rs: the seam and the error vocabulary. Define `pub enum NativeOp` as a CLOSED set with exactly the six variants the sweep pins -- CreateJobObject, SetInformation, QueryInformation, TerminateJob, QueryAccounting, CloseHandle -- with no catch-all or Other variant, so adding an operation is a compile error at every match site rather than a silent fallthrough. Define `pub struct NativeError { op: NativeOp, code: u32 }` carrying ONLY those two fields: per the task rail the error must never echo executable, argv, cwd, environment or raw handle values, and the way that rail is broken in Rust is a derived Debug on a struct that holds a handle -- so no handle, path or string field may exist on this type at all. Define `pub trait Win32Calls` with one method per arm, each returning Result<_, NativeError>, taking and returning an opaque handle newtype rather than a bare isize. Provide `pub struct SystemWin32` implementing it over windows-sys with the unsafe blocks confined to this file, each call mapping a zero/INVALID return to NativeError { op, code: GetLastError() }. Keep the unsafe surface here only; no other module in this crate may contain `unsafe`.
implementationPlan.note:
win32.rs lands and compiles: `cargo build --locked ...` EXIT 0, zero warnings. 246 physical lines (grep -c ''), under the 250 target. `grep -rn unsafe src/ | grep -v win32.rs` -> NONE, so the unsafe surface is confined as required.

I READ THE VENDORED windows-sys 0.61.2 SOURCE RATHER THAN ASSUMING ITS API, and it changed two decisions:

1. **Win32_Security ADDED to features — mandatory, not convenience.** CreateJobObjectW is declared `#[cfg(feature = "Win32_Security")]` because its first parameter is `*const SECURITY_ATTRIBUTES`:
     #[cfg(feature = "Win32_Security")]
     windows_link::link!("kernel32.dll" "system" fn CreateJobObjectW(lpjobattributes : *const super::super::Security::SECURITY_ATTRIBUTES, lpname : PCWSTR) -> HANDLE);
   Without the feature the function does not exist at all. We still pass NULL for that parameter. `Win32_System_JobObjects = ["Win32_System"]` does not pull it in.

2. **JobObjectBasicLimitInformation REPLACES the plan's JobObjectExtendedLimitInformation.** This is a deviation from step 5's wording, forced by task rail 5, and it is the one judgement call in this step:
     #[cfg(feature = "Win32_System_Threading")]
     pub struct JOBOBJECT_EXTENDED_LIMIT_INFORMATION { ... pub IoInfo: super::Threading::IO_COUNTERS, ... }
   The EXTENDED struct embeds Threading::IO_COUNTERS and is therefore gated on Win32_System_Threading — the exact feature risk 7 and task rail 5 forbid adding, because child 2 owns it. The alternatives were: add the forbidden feature, or use the ungated basic path. Measured that the basic path is complete for this task:
     JOBOBJECT_BASIC_LIMIT_INFORMATION  -> UNGATED, has `pub LimitFlags: JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT` (u32)
     JobObjectBasicLimitInformation      = 2   (ungated)
     JOBOBJECT_BASIC_ACCOUNTING_INFORMATION -> UNGATED, has `pub ActiveProcesses: u32`
   KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE is a documented BASIC LimitFlag; only JOB_MEMORY/PROCESS_MEMORY are extended-only, and neither is in scope. So nothing is lost, the feature set stays minimal, and child 2 is free to add Threading and move to the extended struct when it needs IO counters. Recorded in a Cargo.toml comment so the next reader does not "fix" it back.

CONSTANTS VERIFIED AGAINST THE HEADER, NOT MEMORY:
  JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE   = 8192 = 0x2000
  JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_BREAKAWAY_OK        = 2048 = 0x0800
  JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_SILENT_BREAKAWAY_OK = 4096 = 0x1000
REQUIRED_LIMIT_FLAGS is written as the literal 0x2000 and then cross-checked at COMPILE TIME:
  #[cfg(windows)] const _: () = assert!(REQUIRED_LIMIT_FLAGS == ...JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE);
The build passing IS that proof. If windows-sys ever disagrees, the build fails rather than shipping a Job with the wrong bit.

RAIL-2 DEFENCE IS STRUCTURAL. NativeError has exactly two fields (op, code) and no handle/path/string field can exist on it, because the way this rail breaks in Rust is a derived Debug on a struct that holds a handle — not a log statement. Display is hand-written over those two fields only. RawHandle is a newtype so a handle cannot be passed where an exit code or PID is expected, and it is never carried inside NativeError.

NativeOp is closed: six variants, no catch-all, not #[non_exhaustive], so child 2 adding an arm is a compile error at every match site.

Two smaller notes: CreateJobObjectW passes a NULL name deliberately (a named Job is openable by an unrelated process via OpenJobObject) with the reason in a comment; and lib.rs gained `pub mod win32;` plus its re-exports now so this step could compile — step 6 still owns the final surface and the crate-level decision record.

HEADROOM FLAG for step 6 and for child 2: win32.rs is at 246/250. It is compliant now, but child 2 adds arms to this exact file. If step 6's wiring pushes it over, I split the SystemWin32 impl out by responsibility rather than reformatting — and would then have to restate the "unsafe confined to this file" invariant, which is currently written in the module doc comment.

implementationPlan.description: Implement src/handle.rs: RAII that closes exactly once and never launders an uncertain close into success. Define an owned-handle type generic over the call table that holds the raw handle plus a `closed: bool` flag. Provide an explicit `close(self) -> Result<(), NativeError>` that consumes the value, performs the close, sets the flag, and RETURNS the error -- this is the supported path, because Drop cannot return a Result and so can never report a failed close. Drop closes only when the flag is unset, acting purely as a leak guard. State this split in a comment: the reason the explicit close exists is that converting an unknown close outcome into success is exactly what DoD item 6 forbids, and a Drop-only design has no way to avoid doing so. Guarantee close-exactly-once by construction -- the flag plus consuming self makes a double close unrepresentable rather than merely untested -- and let the drop-counting table in the sweep prove it.
implementationPlan.note:
handle.rs lands, compiles clean (EXIT 0, zero warnings), 68 physical lines.

CLOSE-EXACTLY-ONCE IS BY CONSTRUCTION, and it is worth being precise about which mechanism does what, because two different things are being prevented:
- `close(mut self)` CONSUMES the value, so a second EXPLICIT close does not compile. That is the type system, not a test.
- the `closed` flag stops DROP from repeating a close that already ran. That is the runtime half, and it is what the drop-counting table in the sweep actually observes.
Neither alone is sufficient: consuming self does not stop Drop from running after close() returns, and the flag alone would not stop a caller closing twice by hand.

THE ORDERING INSIDE close_once IS THE LOAD-BEARING DETAIL, not an implementation nicety. The flag is set BEFORE the close call, not after:

    self.closed = true;
    self.calls.close_handle(self.raw)

If close fails, its outcome is genuinely UNKNOWN — the handle may or may not have been released. Setting the flag afterwards (only on success) would look more careful and would be wrong: Drop would then retry, and a retry can close a handle the OS already freed, whose numeric value Windows may since have REUSED for an unrelated object. So the attempt is spent either way and the error goes back to the caller. This is the concrete reason the sweep asserts close_count == 1 on the failed-close path rather than >= 1.

WHY TWO CLOSE PATHS EXIST AT ALL, recorded in the module comment so it is not re-litigated: Drop cannot return a Result, so a Drop-only RAII design must discard a failed close, and discarding it converts an unknown cleanup into an implicit success — precisely what DoD item 6 forbids. The explicit consuming close is therefore the supported path and Drop is demoted to a leak guard.

One Rust-specific note for whoever reads this next: `close(mut self)` works without ManuallyDrop only because Drop still runs at the end of close() and finds the flag set. It is not that Drop is skipped — it is that Drop becomes a no-op. Anyone "simplifying" this by moving the field out of self will hit E0509 (cannot move out of a type which implements Drop) and may be tempted to reintroduce a Drop-only design; the module comment says why not to.

lib.rs gained `pub mod handle;` + `pub use handle::OwnedHandle;` to compile this step. Step 6 still owns the final public surface. The sweep remains RED — Job does not exist yet, which is step 5.

implementationPlan.description: Implement src/job.rs: the Job object itself, turning the sweep green. Create the Job with CreateJobObjectW passing a NULL name -- unnamed is required, and a named Job would let an unrelated process open it by name. Set limits via SetInformationJobObject with JobObjectExtendedLimitInformation, LimitFlags set to exactly JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE. Then query the flags back with QueryInformationJobObject and compare with EXACT EQUALITY (`flags == JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE`), never a bitwise-contains test: contains would silently accept a Job that also carries JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_BREAKAWAY_OK or SILENT_BREAKAWAY_OK, which is precisely the configuration the DoD forbids and which would let a child escape the Job. On mismatch refuse with NativeOp::QueryInformation rather than proceeding. Also expose terminate (TerminateJobObject) and an active-process count read via QueryInformationJobObject with JobObjectBasicAccountingInformation, returning ActiveProcesses. Do NOT implement any process creation, JOB_LIST attribute, assignment, membership, identity, resume, wait or unwind behaviour -- those are child 2's (task-a02496064e9e4e87a888cc112830d7a4) and duplicating them here collides with its owner in the shared worktree.

  test every_acquired_handle_closes_exactly_once_on_every_path ... ok
  test a_failed_close_is_never_laundered_into_success ... ok
  test query_back_refuses_flags_that_also_carry_breakaway ... ok

  test result: ok. 7 passed; 0 failed.  EXIT 0

job.rs is 81 lines. Full production budget: win32.rs 246, job.rs 81, handle.rs 67, lib.rs 11 — all under the 250 target.

THE EQUALITY GUARD, written the only way that can reject the dangerous case:
    if observed != REQUIRED_LIMIT_FLAGS { return Err(NativeError::new(NativeOp::QueryInformation, 0)); }
A bitwise-contains (`observed & REQUIRED == REQUIRED`) would ACCEPT a Job that also carries BREAKAWAY_OK or SILENT_BREAKAWAY_OK — a child could then leave the Job and survive it. Step 7 drills exactly this mutation.

CODE 0 ON THE MISMATCH IS DELIBERATE AND WORTH DEFENDING: nothing failed at the Win32 boundary, so there is no GetLastError value to report. Inventing one would be fabricated evidence; reusing the previous call's would be worse. The refusal is ours, and op=QueryInformation names where it was detected.

FIRST-FAILURE PRESERVATION IS STRUCTURAL, not an ordering someone has to maintain. `create` builds the OwnedHandle before calling `configure`, so a set/query failure returns through `?` and the handle closes as the local drops — the drop path CANNOT overwrite the returned error because Drop has no way to return one. The sweep pins the resulting call log as exactly ["create","set","close"], so a refactor that closed before capturing the error, or that returned the close error instead, reddens.

INVARIANT WORTH NAMING FOR CHILD 2: a `Job` value cannot exist unverified. `create` is the only constructor and it returns Err unless the query-back matched exactly, so "configured and verified" is a property of the type, not a step a caller must remember. Child 2 can assume any `Job` it receives is already verified.

SCOPE BOUNDARY MEASURED, NOT ASSERTED. grep across src/ and Cargo.toml for CreateProcess, AssignProcessToJobObject, JOB_LIST, ResumeThread, IsProcessInJob, Win32_System_Threading -> NONE. Child 2's surface is untouched.

Two honesty notes written into the doc comments rather than left implicit, because both are places a later reader could over-claim: `active_processes` is an observation and not proof of tree death (it is only meaningful while this handle is open and says nothing about processes that already left); and a successful `close` is crash-safety via KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE, NOT evidence that contained processes died — once the handle is gone there is nothing left to query.

implementationPlan.description: Mutation-drill every guard, because a sweep whose assertions have detached from their subject stays green (epic rail 6). One at a time, mutate the production source, re-run the exact test command, confirm tests/job_sweep.rs goes RED, then restore the exact bytes. Drill: (a) change the query-back comparison from `==` to a bitwise-contains and confirm the breakaway-flag mismatch case reddens -- this is the highest-value drill in the task, because contains-instead-of-equals is a real escape hatch that a green suite would not otherwise reveal; (b) skip the query-back call entirely; (c) pass a non-NULL name to CreateJobObjectW; (d) swap one NativeOp for another at a failure site and confirm the exact-op assertion reddens, proving the sweep asserts the op and not merely that an error occurred; (e) make the explicit close swallow its error and return Ok, confirming the uncertainty-retention assertion reddens; (f) remove one entry from CASES and confirm the CASES.len() == 6 guard reddens, proving the sweep guard is itself live. In this shared working directory a foreign completion hook can commit your drill edit while `git status` still looks clean -- trust the red test, and verify restoration with `git diff -- packages/runner/src/platform/windows/native/` returning empty rather than with status.
implementationPlan.note:
Six drills run. FIVE REDDENED, ONE SURVIVED — reporting the survivor rather than burying it.

  (a) query-back `==` -> bitwise-contains        RED  1 test: query_back_refuses_flags_that_also_carry_breakaway
  (b) skip the query-back call entirely          RED  4 tests
  (c) non-NULL name to CreateJobObjectW          **SURVIVED — 7/7 still green**
  (d) NativeOp::QueryInformation -> SetInformation at the refusal site   RED  1 test
  (e) explicit close swallows its error, returns Ok                      RED  3 tests
  (f) CASES 6 entries -> 5                                               RED  1 test (the len guard)

(a) is the one that mattered and it behaved exactly right: ONE test reddened, and it was the breakaway case. (d) reddening proves the sweep asserts WHICH op, not merely that an error occurred — a test that only checked `is_err()` would have stayed green under (d). (f) proves the case-list guard is itself live rather than decorative.

DRILL (c) SURVIVED, AND THE REASON GENERALISES: the sweep injects `ScriptedCalls`, so NOTHING in this task's suite executes `SystemWin32`, the real windows-sys binding. That is roughly 118 lines of win32.rs — the NULL-name argument, the info-class choices, the struct sizes and the GetLastError mapping — with ZERO behavioural coverage. The task description puts real-Windows integration tests out of scope (child 2 owns them), so this is a declared boundary and not a defect I introduced. But the honest statement is narrower than "the primitive is mutation-tested": the JOB LOGIC is mutation-tested; the WIN32 BINDING is not tested at all.

Two things do still constrain that binding, and they are worth naming so nobody over- or under-credits it: the compile-time `const _: () = assert!(REQUIRED_LIMIT_FLAGS == JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE)` fails the BUILD if the flag constant is ever wrong, and the type system pins the signatures. Neither can catch a wrong name argument, a wrong JOBOBJECTINFOCLASS, or a wrong size.

CONCRETE HANDOFF REQUIREMENT FOR CHILD 2, since it inherits this gap: its real-Windows acceptance must drive create -> configure -> query-back -> terminate -> close through `SystemWin32`, not only process membership. If it tests only membership and resume, the NULL-name and info-class decisions ship permanently unverified.

THE PLAN'S RESTORE CHECK WOULD HAVE BEEN A FALSE GREEN, and this is the process finding worth keeping. Step 7 says verify restoration with `git diff -- <crate path>` returning empty. This crate is UNTRACKED — `git ls-files <crate>` returns nothing — so `git diff` on that path returns empty ALWAYS, including while a mutation is still sitting in the file. I proved that before drilling rather than after. Used SHA-256 instead: baseline captured up front, pristine copies held OUTSIDE the repo (mktemp -d, so no probe artifact can be swept into a commit), and after every drill `sha256sum -c` re-verified. Final state: 5 of 5 files OK, byte-exact.

Post-restore gate re-run cold: 7 passed, 0 failed, EXIT 0.

implementationPlan.description: Adversarial review, then the gates. Review your own diff as an attacker: can any NativeError, Debug output or panic message carry a handle value, path, argv or environment string? Is NativeOp genuinely closed, with no catch-all? Can a Job be observed in a configured state before the query-back succeeded? Is `unsafe` confined to win32.rs? Can any handle close twice, or a failed close read as success? Then run the exact verification command: `cargo test --locked --manifest-path packages/runner/src/platform/windows/native/Cargo.toml --target-dir dist/windows-job-native -p moe-windows-job-core && cargo build --locked --release --manifest-path packages/runner/src/platform/windows/native/Cargo.toml --target-dir dist/windows-job-native -p moe-windows-job-core` and paste the fresh output as complete_task evidence. --locked will fail if Cargo.lock drifted, which is the intended pin check. ALSO run the Node-side gates `pnpm --filter @moe/runner typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/runner test`, because this crate lands inside an existing Node package's src tree (@moe/runner globs packages/runner/src) and the point of running them is to prove the new non-TypeScript files do not disturb that package; if they are red, apply the path-attributed baseline rail before attributing it here. Finally `git status --porcelain`, confirm no target/, binary, or probe artifact is tracked, and commit by explicit pathspec only: `git commit -- packages/runner/src/platform/windows/native/` , then verify with `git show --stat` that only that subtree landed.
implementationPlan.note:
Adversarial review found TWO REAL HOLES; both fixed before the commit, not filed as follow-ups.

1. **Double-close was reachable from outside the crate.** "Closes exactly once" was a guarantee about one OwnedHandle, NOT about a raw handle value. `OwnedHandle::new` and `raw()` were both public, so a consumer could take `h.raw()` from a live handle and construct a SECOND owner over the same value — both would then close it, and the second close could land on a handle Windows had already reused for an unrelated object. Fixed: both are now `pub(crate)`. Child 2 lives inside this crate, so it loses nothing. The type stays exported as an opaque RAII value with no public constructor.

2. **RawHandle derived Debug.** The no-echo rail does not get broken by a log line; it gets broken by someone adding `#[derive(Debug)]` to a future struct that happens to hold a handle. Removed the derive, so that future derive is now a COMPILE ERROR rather than a silent handle leak — the same forcing function the closed NativeOp uses.

Re-ran drill (a) after both edits: still reddens exactly `query_back_refuses_flags_that_also_carry_breakaway`, job.rs restored byte-exact.

Rest of the checklist, checked not assumed: NativeError has only op+code and hand-written Display; NativeOp is closed with no catch-all; a Job cannot be observed configured before the query-back because `create` is the only constructor and builds the value AFTER `configure` returns Ok; `unsafe` greps to win32.rs only; the error path closes via Drop and cannot overwrite the operational error because Drop returns nothing; no shared mutable state (the only mutation is `closed` behind &mut self on an owned value); GetLastError is read with no intervening Win32 call.

GATES.
Cargo, exact command, fresh after the commit: 7 passed, 0 failed, release profile finished, EXIT 0.

Node-side @moe/runner gates are RED, and the red is FOREIGN — attributed by measurement, not by assertion:
  typecheck: 10 errors, all in packages/runner/src/scope/scope-git.test.ts
  test:      2 files failed / 41 passed, 30 tests failed / 1334 passed
             failing files: src/scope/scope-git.test.ts, src/artifacts/artifact-enumeration.test.ts
Both failing files are UNTRACKED (`git status` -> `??`, `git ls-tree -r HEAD` -> absent), i.e. another agent's in-flight TDD red — scope-git.test.ts imports `parseRefListing`/`listRefs`, which grep confirms do NOT exist in scope-git.ts yet.

My diff is STRUCTURALLY INCAPABLE of causing either: `packages/runner/tsconfig.json` include is `["src/**/*.ts"]`, and every file I own is .rs/.toml/.lock/.gitignore — extension census of my owned tree returns exactly {gitignore, lock, rs, toml}, zero .ts. So the (2)-minus-(1) delta intersected with my owned paths is EMPTY. Disclosed verbatim rather than reported as green.

COMMIT ffa39d6, by explicit pathspec, 9 files / 787 insertions, only my subtree. Index was empty beforehand (checked, since it is shared state). `git add -n` dry run showed no target/, .exe, .pdb or .rlib. Verified the COMMITTED BYTES rather than trusting the diff: `git rev-parse HEAD:<path>` vs `git hash-object <path>` = MATCH on all 9; `git ls-tree -r HEAD | grep -c windows/native` = 9, so no stray duplicate path. Drill backups lived outside the repo and are deleted.

QA audit by qa-b2df68b9, 2026-08-09 ~15:15Z. Approving. Full evidence; the approval summary is the short form.

## Gate re-run by me, both legs

```
cargo test  --locked ... -p moe-windows-job-core   -> 7 passed; 0 failed   EXIT 0
cargo build --locked --release ...                 -> Finished `release`   EXIT 0
```
Matches the reported `verification` exactly. The command was **not narrowed** — no `--exclude`, no test filter, no `|| true`. It is the DoD's own command verbatim.

## DoD coverage

**1 — pins.** `rust-toolchain.toml` `channel = "1.96.0"`. `Cargo.toml` `windows-sys = { version = "=0.61.2" }` — a genuine exact pin; the comment correctly notes a bare `"0.61.2"` would accept 0.61.3. `Cargo.lock` carries `version = "0.61.2"` with checksum `ae137229…f3fc`. Both legs exit 0 on this Windows host.

**2 — artifact hygiene.** `git check-ignore -v dist/windows-job-native` → `.gitignore:4:dist/`. `git ls-files` matching `^dist/|\.exe$|\.pdb$|\.rlib$|/target/` → **empty**. Committed set under `native/` is exactly the 9 intended files. The crate-local `.gitignore` covering `target/` is doing real work, not decoration: the root ignore covers `dist/` but not this crate's own `target/`, so a bare `cargo build` here without `--target-dir` would otherwise leave an untracked-then-committable target tree. The file documents that with the `git check-ignore` output that proves it.

**3 — exact-flags refusal.** `job.rs:71-81`. `set_limit_flags(job, REQUIRED_LIMIT_FLAGS)` → `query_limit_flags` → `if observed != REQUIRED_LIMIT_FLAGS` → `Err(NativeError::new(NativeOp::QueryInformation, 0))`. Exact equality, not contains. `REQUIRED_LIMIT_FLAGS = 0x0000_2000` is held to the real constant by a **compile-time** assertion at `win32.rs:115-119` against `JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE`, so a windows-sys drift fails the build instead of shipping a Job configured with the wrong bit. Code 0 is deliberate and asserted: `"a mismatch is a refusal, not a Win32 failure"`.

**4 — call-table containment and no leakage.** `NativeError { op: NativeOp, code: u32 }` — a closed 6-variant enum plus a numeric code, and nothing else. No `String`, no path, no argv, no raw handle in the type, so leaking one is not merely avoided, it is unrepresentable. `grep -rn windows_sys src/` returns hits in **`win32.rs` only** (4), so `job.rs` and `handle.rs` reach Win32 solely through `C: Win32Calls`.

**5 — sweep.** `CASES: [Case; 6]` with `assert_eq!(CASES.len(), 6, "every failable arm needs exactly one case")` — the nonzero exact case count epic rail 6 demands. Per arm it asserts both `error.op()` and `error.code()`. The reached set is compared against **`NativeOp::ALL`, which lives in the production surface**, not against the test's own `CASES` — with the comment at `:170` saying why ("comparing the sweep to its own input would prove nothing"). That is the global rail's "assert against the production surface, not a test helper that reimplements it", satisfied deliberately rather than by luck.

**6 — close exactly once.** `handle.rs`: `close(mut self)` consumes the value, so a second explicit close **does not compile**; `close_once` sets `closed = true` **before** calling, so a failed close is spent rather than retried against a handle whose value Windows may have reused. `Drop` is a leak guard only and the module comment states plainly why it cannot be the supported path (it cannot return a `Result`, and discarding the outcome would convert an UNKNOWN cleanup into an implicit success — the exact thing DoD 6 forbids). Drop-counting assertions land on all four paths: success `:225`, drop-guard `:230`, refusal `:202` ("refusal must still close the Job"), failed-close `:258` ("failed close was retried by Drop"). `a_failed_close_is_never_laundered_into_success` pins op `CloseHandle` code 998.

**7 — consumer named.** `job.rs:5-8` names child 2 (`task-a02496064e9e4e87a888cc112830d7a4`) as owner of the absent behaviour, in the source rather than only in the ticket. Line counts below.

## Mutation drill — run by me, not read

I ran the drill the worker nominated, **in a copy of the crate outside the repository**, because a foreign completion hook swept another agent's in-flight edit into an unrelated commit earlier today and this crate is now tracked. `job.rs:74` exact equality → bitwise contains:

```
test query_back_refuses_flags_that_also_carry_breakaway ... FAILED
panicked at tests\job_sweep.rs:198:43: mismatched flags must refuse
test result: FAILED. 6 passed; 1 failed
```
Red on exactly one test, the right one, with a message that names the property. That is the defect whose survival a green suite would never announce — contains would accept a Job also carrying `BREAKAWAY_OK`, letting a child leave the Job and survive it.

Temp copy deleted. Repo verified untouched afterwards: `git status --porcelain` on the crate is empty, `job.rs:74` still reads `!=`, and all 9 files verified `git rev-parse HEAD:<path>` == `git hash-object <path>`.

## The one DoD item not literally met — disclosed, not waived quietly

**`src/win32.rs` is 252 physical lines** (`grep -c ''` and `wc -l` agree; file ends with a newline). DoD 7 says "Every Rust production source is <=250 physical lines". The others: `lib.rs` 46, `handle.rs` 77, `job.rs` 81.

I am approving over this and stating why rather than burying it. All three rails that govern it define 250 as a **target** and 400 as the enforcement bar — global ("Target <=250 physical lines per production source; split before 400"), epic rail 5, and task rail 3 ("target <=250 physical lines and split before 400"). DoD 7 restated the target in the grammar of a hard bar. The file is **148 lines under the enforcement bar**, and its census is 155 code / 68 comment / 29 blank — so the 2-line overage sits entirely inside documentation, and the cheapest literal fix is deleting two comment lines that the rails elsewhere reward keeping.

@governor-f70d1157 — this is the one call here a governor might make differently. If DoD 7's `<=250` is meant as a hard bar for this task rather than a restatement of the rail's target, say so and I will reopen; the honest fix in that case is extracting `NativeOp`/`NativeError` into their own module, which would be a real improvement rather than comment-shaving.

## Not defects, recorded so they are not rediscovered

- **Surviving mutant, disclosed by the worker.** Passing a non-NULL name to `CreateJobObjectW` leaves 7/7 green, because the sweep injects a scripted call table and nothing here executes `SystemWin32`. The task description names real-Windows tests as child 2's scope, so this is a declared boundary. The accurate claim is the worker's own: *the Job logic is mutation-tested; the Win32 binding is not tested at all*.
- **Plan deviation, justified.** `JOBOBJECT_BASIC_LIMIT_INFORMATION` instead of the extended struct, because the extended one is `#[cfg(feature = "Win32_System_Threading")]` and task rail 5 fences that feature to child 2. `KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE` is a documented basic `LimitFlags` bit. `Win32_Security` was added because `CreateJobObjectW` is gated on it. Both recorded in Cargo.toml comments.
- **Consequence child 2 must inherit.** Those two combine: the info-class deviation is exactly the kind of decision only real-Windows execution can validate, and nothing in this task executes the binding. Child 2's DoD should explicitly require asserting that `KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE` set through `JobObjectBasicLimitInformation` actually terminates on last-handle-close. If it only inherits "test on real Windows", the deviation never gets checked — a Cargo.toml comment records a decision, it does not schedule its verification.
- **Foreign red, attribution confirmed independently.** `pnpm --filter @moe/runner typecheck` is red on `src/scope/scope-git.test.ts` (TS2305/TS2339/TS7006) and `src/artifacts/artifact-enumeration.test.ts`. Both are **untracked** and absent from `git ls-tree HEAD` — another agent's in-flight TDD red. I hit the same file reviewing task-36ac4b43 from the opposite direction. The owned tree's extension census is `{gitignore, lock, rs, toml}` with zero `.ts` against a tsconfig including `src/**/*.ts`, so this diff cannot have caused it. Delta ∩ owned paths = EMPTY.

planSizeWarnings: Plan touches 9 distinct files (target <=5); plans over 10 are rejected. Small file-disjoint tasks review better and parallelize.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
WHY THIS TASK EXISTS AS A CHILD. The parent task-ea76e0cf9bdb4f1888aaa9e49323c782 was split on PLAN SHAPE, never on lines (epic rail 5 forbids splitting on task-level LOC). A single plan needs 12 distinct files against the daemon's hard ceiling of 10, and ~11-12 steps against the ceiling of 12. It can be forced to exactly 10 files only by merging the Job and process concerns into modules that would each land well past the 250-line per-file target on dense unsafe Win32 code -- so the squeeze would trade a shape violation for a per-file violation, which is the one the rails enforce strictly. The two halves are also genuinely separable: making a correctly configured Job, versus putting a process inside it and proving membership before it can run.

CALL TABLE OVER CONDITIONAL COMPILATION. Rejected: #[cfg(test)] shims or a mock crate. Every Win32 arm must be independently failure-injectable to satisfy the sweep, and cfg-gated fakes mean the tested code is not the shipped code. Chosen: a Win32Calls trait with a real SystemWin32 implementation and a scripted test table, so the production path under test is the production path.

CLOSED ENUM, NO CATCH-ALL. Rejected: a NativeOp with an Other(u32) or #[non_exhaustive] variant. A catch-all turns 'we added an operation and forgot to classify it' into a silent runtime fallthrough; a closed set turns it into a compile error at every match site. Child 2 adds variants deliberately, which is exactly when the compiler should force a review of every site.

EXPLICIT close() PLUS Drop LEAK-GUARD. Rejected: Drop-only RAII. Drop cannot return a Result, so a Drop-only design has no way to report a failed close and must silently discard it -- which is precisely the conversion of an uncertain cleanup into success that DoD item 6 forbids. Chosen: a consuming `close(self) -> Result<(), NativeError>` as the supported path, with Drop closing only if that never ran. Close-exactly-once is then guaranteed by construction (consuming self plus a flag) rather than merely asserted.

EXACT EQUALITY ON THE QUERY-BACK. Rejected: testing the flags with a bitwise-contains. Contains would accept a Job that ALSO carries JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_BREAKAWAY_OK or SILENT_BREAKAWAY_OK -- the exact configuration that lets a child escape the Job and defeats the whole primitive. The comparison is `==`, and step 7 drills it specifically.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
ALL PREREQUISITES MEASURED 2026-08-09 AT HEAD 7d9efc9, none taken from the description (epic stale-by-default rail).

- `ls -d packages/runner/src/platform/windows/native` -> No such file or directory. The gap is real; this is greenfield.
- `find . -name Cargo.toml -not -path '*/node_modules/*'` -> EMPTY. **This is the first Rust in the monorepo.** There is no existing crate, workspace, CI cargo step or toolchain file to follow, so every convention in this plan is being established rather than matched.

So the registry is reachable, version =0.61.2 exists, and the Win32_System_JobObjects feature name is correct. The probe directory was deleted.

But `git check-ignore` on the crate's own `target/` path returns NOTHING. That asymmetry is why step 1 adds a crate-local .gitignore: a developer who runs a bare `cargo build` without --target-dir would otherwise produce a tracked target directory and violate DoD item 2.

Neither tool matches .rs files, so no interference is expected -- but step 8 runs both anyway, because "expected" is not measured.
planningNotes.risks:
1. THE HIGHEST-VALUE DRILL IS THE EQUALITY ONE. A bitwise-contains query-back passes every naive test and silently permits a breakaway-capable Job. Drill (a) in step 7 exists for this and must be seen to redden.

2. THE ERROR TYPE IS WHERE THE NO-ECHO RAIL BREAKS. In Rust the rail is not broken by a log statement, it is broken by `#[derive(Debug)]` on a struct that happens to hold a handle or a path. NativeError must carry ONLY the op and the numeric code, with no handle, string or path field in the type at all. Check panic and assert messages in the tests too.

3. FIRST RUST IN THE REPO -- NO PRECEDENT TO COPY. There is no existing crate, CI cargo step or lint config. Do not invent repo-wide Rust tooling, a workspace Cargo.toml at the repo root, or a CI change; this task owns one crate directory and nothing else. A root workspace member list is explicitly NOT in scope.

4. THE UNIGNORED target/ PATH. dist/ is ignored, the crate's own target/ is not. If a bare `cargo build` is ever run in the crate directory without --target-dir, a tracked target tree appears and DoD item 2 fails. The crate-local .gitignore in step 1 is the guard; do not skip it as cosmetic.

5. --locked IS A REAL GATE, NOT A FLAG. It fails if Cargo.lock does not match Cargo.toml. Generate the lock in step 1 and commit it; if a later step edits dependencies, the lock must be regenerated in the same step or the final gate fails for a reason unrelated to the code.

6. SHARED WORKING DIRECTORY. All agents work in D:/projexts/moe-next. During the step-7 drills another task's completion hook can commit a tree containing your live mutation, leaving git status clean while the mutation is still in the file. Trust the red test; verify restoration with `git diff -- <crate path>` returning empty.

7. SCOPE BOUNDARY WITH CHILD 2. Do not add Win32_System_Threading to the feature list, and do not implement CreateProcessW, PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_JOB_LIST, AssignProcessToJobObject, membership, identity, ResumeThread, wait or unwind. task-a02496064e9e4e87a888cc112830d7a4 owns all of it and will edit win32.rs and lib.rs to add its arms.

8. WINDOWS-ONLY CRATE. The dependency is declared under [target.'cfg(windows)'.dependencies]. The task is verified on Windows; do not add a non-Windows fallback implementation, which would be untested authority.
